nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of NF was sonicated in 3 M HCl for 15 min to remove the oxide layer on the NF surface. Then, the NF was cleaned by ultrasonication in water and ethanol sequentially for 5 min to remove residual contaminants on the surface. And then dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C for 12 h to obtain fresh NF.
nodes.source_text: First, a piece of NF was sonicated in 3 M HCl for 15 min... dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C for 12 h to obtain fresh NF.

nodes.name: ZIF-L Growth on NF
nodes.procedure: 40 mL 0.4 M 2-Methylimidazole (C4H6N2) aqueous solution was quickly added to 40 mL 0.05 m cobalt nitrate hexahydrate (Co(NO3)2·6H2O) aqueous solution. The dried nickel foam was placed into the mixture solution, slowly stirred to react at room temperature for 4 h and then was taken out, washed with deionized water and dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C for 12 h to obtain ZIF-L@NF.
nodes.source_text: 40 mL 0.4 M 2-Methylimidazole aqueous solution was quickly added to 40 mL 0.05 m cobalt nitrate hexahydrate aqueous solution... dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C for 12 h to obtain ZIF-L@NF.

nodes.name: WO4^2-/Co-LDH Formation
nodes.procedure: 0.6 g of Sodium Tungstate Dihydrate (Na2WO4) was dissolved into a mixture of deionized water and ethanol (water:ethanol = 4:1), then the dried ZIF-L@NF was placed into the mixture solution, etched at 85 °C for 15 min and then taken out, washed with deionized water and dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C for 12 h to obtain WO4^2-/Co-LDH-6@NF WO4^2-. For comparison, the amount of Na2WO4 added was varied to 0 g, 0.3 g, and 0.9 g and the other preparation methods were the same, to obtain Co-LDH@NF, WO4^2-/Co-LDH-3@NF, WO4^2--/Co-LDH-9@NF.

nodes.name: WO3/CoP Phosphatization
nodes.procedure: A prepared piece of WO4^2-/Co-LDH-x@NF was placed in a porcelain boat, another porcelain boat containing 400 mg of sodium hypophosphite powder was placed on the upstream side of the tube furnace. The tube furnace center was heated to 350 °C at a ramp rate of 2 °C min^-1, held for 2 h, and cooled naturally to room temperature in N2 atmosphere, to obtain WO3/CoP-X on NF.
nodes.source_text: A prepared piece of WO4^2-/Co-LDH-x@NF was placed in a porcelain boat... to obtain WO3/CoP-X on NF.

nodes.name: CoP@NF Phosphatization
nodes.procedure: Using the same conditions [as WO3/CoP], Co-LDH@NF was phosphated to obtain CoP@NF.
nodes.source_text: Using the same conditions, Co-LDH@NF was phosphated to obtain CoP@NF.

nodes.name: WO3@NF Hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: 3 mmol Na2WO4·2H2O was dissolved in 70 mL deionized water, and concentrated hydrochloric acid was added into the solution until the pH value of the solution was adjusted to 1.5. Subsequently, 3 mmol NaCl and 3 mmol oxalic acid were added into the obtained solution with stirring for 30 min. The mixed solution was transferred into a Teflon-lined autoclave with a piece of clean nickel NF and heated at 120 °C for 48 h to obtain WO3@NF.
nodes.source_text: 3 mmol Na2WO4·2H2O was dissolved in 70 mL deionized water... heated at 120 °C for 48 h to obtain WO3@NF.

nodes.name: CoP Hydrothermal Precursor
nodes.procedure: 4 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 20 mmol NH4F, and 3.18 g urea were added to 60 mL H2O in order under continuous magnetic agitation to produce a mixed dark red solution. The above solution was transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave with a piece of cleaned NF (3×4 cm²), and kept at 120 °C for 6 h. After cooled to ambient temperature, the reacted NF was taken out and washed by deionized water and dried at 60 °C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: 4 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 20 mmol NH4F, and 3.18 g urea were added to 60 mL H2O... dried at 60 °C for 12 h.

nodes.name: WO3+CoP Physical Mixture
nodes.procedure: The powder obtained from sonicating CoP@NF was mixed with hydrothermally synthesized WO3 powder and thoroughly ground to achieve homogeneity. Subsequently, 10 mg of the resulting mixed powder was used to prepare an ink following the same method, which was then coated onto a clean nickel foam (NF) to obtain WO3+CoP@NF.
nodes.source_text: The powder obtained from sonicating CoP@NF was mixed with hydrothermally synthesized WO3 powder... coated onto a clean nickel foam (NF) to obtain WO3+CoP@NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show agglomerated nanofold-like morphologies for WO₃/CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subsequent phosphatization treatment at 350 °C for 2 h resulted in the formation of agglomerated nanofold-like morphologies (Fig. 1b, c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.247 nm and 0.282 nm corresponding to (111) and (011) planes of crystalline CoP, with a disordered amorphous WO₃ overlayer of average thickness 4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) provided direct evidence for the formation of a heterojunction interface. As shown in Fig. 1e, the lattice fringes with the spacing of 0.247 nm and 0.282 nm are observed, corresponding to the (111) and (011) planes of crystalline CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern exhibits diffraction rings indexed to (011), (111), (211), and (020) planes of CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 1d) exhibits clear diffraction rings indexed to the (011), (111), (211), and (020) planes of CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of P, Co, O, W, and C within WO₃/CoP; TEM-EDS line-scan shows W and O enrichment in surface amorphous layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping (Fig. 1f) results confirm the uniform distribution of P, Co, O, W, and C within ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 } / { \sf C o P }$.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP analysis verifies atomic ratio of Co:W is 1:0.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis verifies that the atomic ratio of Co:W is 1:0.5 (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD shows diffraction peaks indexed to CoP (JCPDS #65-2593) with no detectable crystalline tungsten phases, confirming amorphous WO₃; slight positive peak shift indicates lattice strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 } / { \sf C o P }$ ... exhibits diffraction peaks indexed to standard CoP structure (JCPDS #65–2593), while no detectable crystalline tungsten-based phases are observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows characteristic W-O stretching peak at 946 cm⁻¹ and higher I_D/I_G ratio indicating more defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy provides further insights into the chemical bonds and defect structure. As shown in Fig. S13, CoP exclusively displays Co-O modes, whereas ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 } / { \sf C o P }$ shows a characteristic W-O stretching peak at 946 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR exhibits characteristic W-O stretching vibrations at 561 cm⁻¹ and 918 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the FTIR spectrum of ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 } / { \sf C o P }$ exhibits characteristic peaks at 561 cm⁻¹ and 918 cm⁻¹, which can be attributed to W-O stretching vibrations.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p peaks show Co-P at 778.73/793.74 eV and Co-O at 782.02/798.51 eV with 0.4 eV positive shift vs CoP; P 2p shows Co-P at 128.28/130.57 eV and P-O at 134.19 eV; W 4f shows W-O at 36.23/38.52 eV; XPS depth profiling confirms W surface enrichment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was then employed to analyze the surface composition and bonding states of the catalysts (Fig. 2b-d, Fig. S15, Table S3-4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES locates between Co foil and CoO (average Co valence 0 to +2), with higher energy and stronger white-line intensity for WO₃/CoP indicating electron transfer from Co to W; W L₃-edge between W⁴⁺ and W⁶⁺ (approaching +6 valence).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge XANES spectra of ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 } / { \sf C o P }$ and CoP locate between those of Co foil and standard CoO, indicating that the average valence state of Co ranges from 0 to +2 (Fig. 2e, Fig. 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge R-space shows atomic spacing 1.59 Å (shorter than CoP 1.65 Å) indicating Co-O bonds; W L₃-edge shows first-shell W-O coordination, no W-W bonds, confirming amorphous WO₃ phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The local chemical environment of Co is shown in Fig. 2h, where it can be seen that the atomic spacing of ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 } / { \sf C o P }$ (1.59) is slightly lower compared to that of CoP (1.65).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET measurements show increase in specific surface area and pore volume after reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) measurements before and after the reaction (Fig. S36) reveal an increase in specific surface area and pore volume.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS (after 100 h) shows disappearance of Co 2p Co-P peaks with emergence of Co³⁺ at 780.4/795.3 eV, absence of P 2p Co-P signals, lower W valence state, and intensified O 1s metal oxide/hydroxide peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Post-OER samples were characterized by XPS to analyze elemental valence changes of ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 } / { \sf C o P }$ after 100 h OER testing (Fig. S31 and Table S10).
